claims.text: Yemen's Houthis launched drone and missile attacks against four southern Saudi cities on Tuesday, September 8, setting oil installations on fire and wounding dozens.
Saudi authorities reported that 73 people, including women and children, were hurt in the Houthi attacks across southern Saudi Arabia.
US forces struck multiple Iranian tankers linked to the IRGC after Iranian attempts to hit a US Navy warship.
Iranian state media reported that a US missile struck an Iranian oil tanker 6km from Kharg Island and attacked another near Jask on the Gulf of Oman.
The IRGC warned crews aboard oil tankers in Kuwaiti and Bahraini ports to evacuate immediately, threatening to target the vessels.
The US Treasury announced new aviation-related sanctions aimed at grounding Iranian airlines.
Iran's IRGC stated it captured a US submersible near the Strait of Hormuz, while a US official said a defective underwater military drone had malfunctioned.
US officials told CNN that US strikes targeted multiple Iranian oil tankers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps near Kharg Island on Tuesday.
The Trump administration imposed sanctions targeting 27 Iranian airlines and nine service providers accused of supporting Mahan Air.
Iranian Armed Forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi warned that any attack on Iranian oil tankers would trigger strikes against US bases across the region.
The IRGC claimed it intercepted and destroyed an MQ-1 drone over the Strait of Hormuz using a new Iranian air defence system.
International benchmark Brent crude briefly reached $99.46 a barrel on Tuesday amid rising Gulf tensions.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that talks with Oman on managing the Strait of Hormuz had achieved significant progress.
Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon on Monday killed 13 people, according to the Lebanese Health Ministry.
US Navy Capt Tim Hawkins stated that a defective older-model US drone surveillance submersible malfunctioned in regional waters and contained no sensitive data or classified radar equipment.
The conflict has claimed the lives of 18 US service members.
Fighting between government forces and Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen is raising fears of a return to full-scale war.
Twelve countries, including Britain, France, Spain, and Canada, acted together in introducing or considering measures against trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank.
Israel ordered the closure of the UK's consulate in East Jerusalem and removed British representatives from the International Gaza Support Centre.
The UK government banned goods from Israeli West Bank settlements, restricted services to settlements, and placed limits on arms sales that contribute to the occupation.
British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband stated that settler terrorism in parts of the West Bank amounted to ethnic cleansing of Palestinians while the Israeli government turned a blind eye.
Palestinian ambassador Dr Husam Zomlot called the British government's trade decision a turning point in the UK-Palestine relationship.
Israel announced the shutdown of the UK Consulate in occupied East Jerusalem following Britain's ban on settlement goods.
Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar announced retaliatory measures against the UK, including entry bans on 12 Britons such as former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn and 10 MPs.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated that targeted measures were brought forward not against the Israeli people, but in support of a two-state solution.
UK Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch criticized the British government's decision to ban settlement trade and accused the Labour government of antisemitism.
Britain, France, and Canada announced trade restrictions blocking imports from Israeli West Bank settlements.
Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand stated on X that illegal settlements in the West Bank significantly undermine long-term peace objectives.
France cited the frenzied expansion of settlements and a flare-up of violence as its rationale for banning West Bank settlement goods.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated Washington will not follow Britain, France, and Canada in blocking imports from Israeli settlements.
Israel announced plans for 1,000 new West Bank homes on Tuesday.

Aluminum Association of Canada President Jean Simard stated that US industrial demand substantially exceeds domestic production capacity, making tariffs ineffective at reducing Canadian aluminum in the US market.
Donald Trump threatened to block Canadian aircraft maker Bombardier from selling in the US market unless it moves manufacturing to the United States.
Bombardier employs over 3,000 people in the US and works with roughly 2,800 American companies across 47 states.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney noted that Canada is the largest customer for US goods in 26 states.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney stated in a video address that Canada's trade pivot away from the US will come at a cost but is necessary to protect Canadian workers.
Canada's counter-tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% came into force on Tuesday, targeting nearly C$28 billion ($20 billion) worth of American goods.
The US maintains a 25% tariff on Canadian cars, trucks, steel, aluminium, and lumber, alongside 50% tariffs imposed in late August on Canadian dairy, alcohol, hockey sticks, and perfume.
Canada lost roughly 41,000 jobs in August following the collapse of trade negotiations and new US tariffs.
Canada's retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on around $20 billion of US goods went into effect at midnight on Tuesday.
The Gordie Howe International Bridge connecting Detroit, Michigan and Windsor, Ontario opened recently without US officials attending the event.
The Financial Accountability Office of Ontario estimated the new tariff regime will cost 119,000 local jobs in Ontario in 2026.
US consumers faced record average new car sales prices exceeding $52,000 in September.
US President Donald Trump held an hour-long phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday, stating he wanted a swift end to the war in Ukraine.
The Putin-Trump call followed a weekend visit to Moscow and Kyiv by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov stated that Vladimir Putin told Donald Trump that Russia has no aggressive plans towards European states.
Yuri Ushakov described the hour-long telephone call between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin as constructive and quite frank.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy thanked Donald Trump for allowing US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to visit Ukraine despite ongoing fighting.
Russian strikes on Tuesday morning killed at least five civilians and wounded 25 others in Kyiv, while Ukrainian attacks caused casualties in Bryansk, Kursk, and Crimea.
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday for over three hours before traveling to Kyiv on Sunday.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated following talks with US envoys that he did not see a quick end to the conflict.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that the peace ideas presented by US envoy Jared Kushner included a couple of very good, worthwhile ideas.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed hope to meet Donald Trump around September 20 during the UN General Assembly in New York.
UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting stated Ukraine requires 300 Patriot missiles, 500 air-to-air interceptors, and $2 billion for additional drones.
The European Commission approved a 3.2 billion euro ($3.7 billion) loan for Kyiv to purchase components for Patriot air defence systems.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov stated that Russia remains confident in its military potential and believes victory is very close on the battlefield.
The Institute for the Study of War reported that Russian forces will not seize Donetsk until 2032 at their current rate of advance.
